findings.text: follow-on: FleetState.pointers is built from the same runs.list_live loop and one-line dict comprehension that obligations() writes inline at reckon/crew/obligations.py:647, so the run-id to pointer mapping the two readers both need now has two copies that can drift; sharing one builder would keep the parity the change exists to establish.

item_verdicts.diff: read 4a9d1f7a9 against b63fd85ff; 92 insertions and 18 deletions across exactly reckon/crew/obligation_snapshot.py and tests/test_obligations_snapshot_is_published.py, no file outside that pair.
item_verdicts.done_when: the done-when names both parity cases passing at the merged head plus a moved-head case asserting the snapshot and the derivation name the same two heads; the manifest records base arm 2 failed / 33 passed at b63fd85ff, head arm 36 passed at 4a9d1f7a9, and negative-control-2.log 3 failed / 33 passed with the moved-head case among the failures.
item_verdicts.goal: the goal is that the snapshot's review duties are built through the derivation's own review-duty function; payload_for now routes every REVIEW_CLASSIFICATION_KINDS row through module._review_duty_item, the function obligations() uses, passing the live pointer carried on the snapshot's fleet state, so both readers build the same duty.
item_verdicts.manifest: read; status complete, baseline_suite and after_suite both carry completed true with matching failure sets (base 2 ids, head none), and the landing line states the gate figure.
item_verdicts.write_paths: the diff touches exactly the two declared write paths; reckon/crew/obligations.py was in scope and correctly left unmodified, and changed_paths lists the two files the diff changes.

justifications.durability: the two parity cases pin the snapshot's duty list equal to the derivation's field for field, and the new moved-head case fails under the declared mutation (negative-control-2.log: 3 failed / 33 passed, test_a_moved_head_names_the_same_two_heads among them), so a regression to the snapshot's own duty path is caught rather than silently agreeing.
justifications.evidence: the gate the done-when names ran at both arms (base-arm-2.log: 2 failed / 33 passed, EXIT=1, the two parity cases; head-arm-2.log: 36 passed, EXIT=0) and the base log shows the defect as a review-missing duty whose snapshot row lacks the head pair; I re-ran the snapshot test file independently in the reviewed tree (independent-head-arm.log: 12 passed, EXIT=0).
justifications.fit: the change follows the module's idiom, removes the now-redundant scoring and promotable branches from _duty_kind and documents the split, but the run-id to pointer mapping is now built twice (reckon/crew/obligation_snapshot.py:561 and reckon/crew/obligations.py:647).
justifications.goal_fidelity: reckon/crew/obligation_snapshot.py:616-625 builds a REVIEW_CLASSIFICATION_KINDS row through module._review_duty_item with the run's pointer, the same call obligations() makes at reckon/crew/obligations.py:663, preserving the scoring-in-flight skip and the promotable-stale grace, which is exactly section 9's done-when.
justifications.scope_discipline: every path in the diff is a declared write path, the change is one commit, and ruff check and ruff format --check report no finding on the two changed files.
